title: se role definition
description: YAML frontmatter contract for a role file under se/agents/<department>/. Validation is fail-closed: an unknown key is an error, never a warning, so a typo can never silently disable a role. See docs/origin-prompt.md Part IV 7.2.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier. Never reused, never renamed; retire with status instead.

tier.description: starter carries all 16 sections; catalogue carries the mandatory subset. Part IV 7.1.

mission.description: One or two sentences. If it cannot be stated this briefly the role is not bounded.

activation.description: Project facts that activate this role. Never 'always' for a catalogue role; activation requires a fact, not a hunch.

tools.description: Allowlist of capabilities, closed against vocabulary.json#/capabilities. An unknown term is dropped by every renderer, so it must fail validation rather than silently remove authority.

memory_scopes.description: Deny-by-default. A scope absent from 'read' is unreadable. 'write' to organization or role scope additionally requires human promotion (Part XX 75).

owns_artifacts.description: Accountable ownership. Exactly one enabled role may own an artifact kind unless shared_with declares otherwise. Part XII 47.

contributes_artifacts.description: Contribution without accountability. Unlimited roles may contribute.

shared_with.description: artifact_kind -> role ids with declared co-ownership. Must be reciprocal; one-sided declarations are rejected.

collaborators.description: Role ids. Every id must resolve; a dangling collaborator is a broken handoff.

escalates_to.description: A role id, or 'operator' for decisions reserved to the human.

context_budget_tokens.description: Enforced before invocation, not measured after. Part XI 46.

status.description: Deprecated roles keep their id forever. Part XVII 65.

boundary.description: Required when another role is adjacent. States what this role is NOT, naming the neighbour. An overlapping role is worse than a missing one.

requires_evidence.description: When true, this role cannot report status 'verified' without recorded evidence carrying an exit code. Part IX 40.

writes_files.description: When true, the role requires an isolated workspace to run in parallel. Part XV 53.

owns_spec_sections.description: Sections of the specification this role is accountable for. Used to prove every requirement in Parts IX-XX has an owner.

participates_interfaces.description: Interfaces this role takes part in without owning. Ownership is accountability; participation is not.

verify_commands.description: The commands that prove this role's work. Hardcoded per role rather than inferred, because a role that guesses its own verification command gets it wrong on any non-standard project and then reports the exit code as a failure of the code under test.

escalates_on_failure_to.description: Where stuck work goes, which is a different question from where decisions go. Separate from escalates_to on purpose.

stack_aware.description: When true, renderers append the project's stack-discipline guidance to this role's prompt.

blocked_on.description: Declared gaps: capabilities or commands this role needs that do not exist yet. Declaring the gap is what keeps verify_commands honest.

failure_modes.description: Durable domain failure modes: what breaks in this role's area and the invariant that catches it. Not framework APIs -- those are read from the lockfile at point of use.

mode.description: The observable symptom, not the cause.

guard.description: The check or property that catches it.

lead.description: True for the single role accountable for this department. A routing destination for work spanning several of the department's roles, not an extra delegation layer.
